title: In painted chambers loaded with tilebooks.
html_source:
from Richard Jeffries’s The Story of my Heart: An Autobiography.

This reference was only recently identified, in 2008 (Bliss,R. James Joyce Quarterly, vol 46, no 1).

Jeffries argues that nothing exists of many ancient cultures—since nothing survived of them, why should anything come of our assumed high cultures now?

With relevance to Stephen’s debate he goes on to say:

Turn, then, to the calm reasoning of Aristotle; is there anything in that? Can the half-divine thought of Plato, rising in storeys of sequential ideas, following each other to the conclusion, endure here? No! All the philosophers in Diogenes Laertius fade away: the theories of medieval days; the organon of experiment; down to this hour, they are useless alike.

anchor.text: In painted chambers loaded with tilebooks.
anchor.prefix:
en. 

 Coffined thoughts around me, in mummycases, embalmed in spice of words. Thoth, god of libraries, a birdgod, moonycrowned. And I heard the voice of that Egyptian highpriest.
anchor.suffix:
They are still. Once quick in the brains of men. Still: but an 1961#193itch of 1932#173death is in them, to tell me in my ear a maudlin tale, urge me to wreak their will. 

 —
